why: `bin/cairn rehearse <T> --decide <step> "<line>"` always APPENDS a new line D(n+1) (cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py:691 decide(): n = 1 + max(n)); <step> is only a label, so `--decide D4 "..."` reads like 'amend D4' and lands D(n+1) with step 'D4'. Superseding a line then needs --retire D4 --into D<m>, and retire refuses while any live line's TEXT matches \bD4\b (rehearsal.py:749-751: 'D13 still cites D4 — retire or re-decide it too'), so a refolded line labelled or worded 'D4:' blocks the very retire it was written for. Measured 2026-10-08 on 996668eceef1: `--decide "prompt.md"` landed D12, `--decide D4` landed D13, retire D4 refused citing D13; way through was retire D12+D13, decide D14 without the string 'D4', retire D4 into D14 — three wasted lines on the ticket. Either --decide grows a --supersedes <n> that retires in the same act, or the step label is refused when it is shaped like a decision id.
